item.title: Israeli president invites Netanyahu's opposition leader to broker new government
item.description: Israel's political landscape shifts as President Herzog hands opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot the mandate to form a government, dealing a blow to Benjamin Netanyahu's grip on power.

item.title: Texas's 'Blue Tsunami' has former Texas congressman Beto O'Rourke 'over the moon'
item.description: NPR's Rob Schmitz speaks with former Texas congressman Beto O'Rourke about how past efforts by him and other Democrats helped the party win big in Texas in the midterms.

item.title: The surprising and often forgotten history of economic populism in Texas
item.description: NPR's Rob Schmitz speaks with Austin-based political commentator David Griscom. He authored a book titled The Myth of Red Texas which tells the story of economic populism in Texas.

item.description: Reporting from Cuba comes with distinct challenges especially amid widespread power outages and fuel shortages.

item.title: How painter Maira Kalman finds 'Joy' in darkness
item.description: Author and painter Maira Kalman is out with a new book called Joy, exploring all the things that bring her fleeting happiness and why sorrow is a necessary counterpart to joy.

item.title: President of The Heritage Foundation looks ahead to the future of the GOP
item.description: Kevin Roberts, the president of the conservative think tank The Heritage Foundation, talks about the organization's priorities and hopes for the future of the Republican Party and its policies.

item.title: Oklahoma tribes say proposed legal changes put ancestral lands in Ohio at risk
item.description: The Trump administration has proposed changes to the National Historic Preservation Act that could endanger historic sites significant to tribal nations across the country. Oklahoma tribes say that puts ancestral lands in Ohio at risk.
